clue.text: Passed Peregrine a black suit

indicators.note: peregrine means wandering or travelling, so the word before it roams into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A man called Peregrine walks by wearing a dark suit of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Peregrine looks like a man's name, but as an adjective it means wandering, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the two black suits are clubs and spades, so spades is one of them.

clue.text: Benefit office where pumps may be used

parts.note: a service is a benefit or good turn
a station is a post or position, an office

explanation.surface: A welfare office equipped with pumps, perhaps for something like a blood bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pumps' may suggest shoes, but these are petrol pumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A service station sells fuel from petrol pumps, so motorists use the pumps there.

clue.text: Shock with pointless petition

indicators.note: pointless means lacking a compass point, so one is removed

parts.note: an appeal is a petition

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by a futile petition.
explanation.walkthrough: The point removed is E, for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay, to shock someone deeply.

clue.text: Letter from student in top European skiing area

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, placed at the top of this down answer

indicators.note: in places the student inside the skiing area

parts.note: a piste is a ski run
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A postcard sent home by a student at a leading Alpine ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The student goes inside the ski run, after the opening E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, like the New Testament letters of the apostles.

clue.text: Male star's new suit

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters before it are formed afresh

parts.note: the male pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leading man has had a new suit made for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the male and the star together are new, that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a standard pack of playing cards, alongside clubs, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Flight departure

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a leaving or getting away

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like an airport board; flight means fleeing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape covers both fleeing from danger and getting away from a place.

clue.text: About to go home by midnight — is coming back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to turn in is to go to bed, to retire for the night
the middle of night, its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone planning to head home by twelve o'clock is on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' looks like a time, but splits into mid and night.
explanation.definitionFit: Returning means coming back to a place one has left.

clue.text: Rate other gases differently, but they keep you warm

indicators.note: differently means in another way, so the letters take another order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A scientist ranks the various gases in an alternative way.
explanation.walkthrough: Storage heaters store heat overnight on cheap electricity and release it by day, common in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage heaters are electric room heaters, so they are things that keep you warm.

clue.text: Dresses said disloyal person after commercial manager

indicators.note: after places the dresses and the traitor sound behind the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
minis are short dresses

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a traitor is a disloyal person

explanation.surface: Accusations about a fashion manager who betrayed the firm after an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken ending of the answer sounds like traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator runs or manages an organisation's affairs, so is a manager.

clue.text: Gratuity is about right for an excursion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the next

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity given for service
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tip is appropriate when going on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey made for pleasure, which is what an excursion is.

clue.text: In one state police rejected evidence

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places what follows inside the phrase it governs, here the one state

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the police abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Within one American state, the police have thrown out the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The police go backwards inside I plus NATION, splitting it after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign or token pointing to something, much as evidence suggests a conclusion.

clue.text: Venture round sick quarters

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: to venture money is to bet it
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Taking a risk around the sickbay or the infirmary's quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging for soldiers, so it means quarters in the military housing sense.

clue.text: August, the end of June and April I'm travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the collected letters move into a new order
the end of asks for only the final letter of the month named

parts.note: last letter of the month
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone lists the summer and spring months they will spend on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: August opens the clue with a capital, so it reads as the month, but here it is the adjective meaning majestic.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand and dignified, the regal quality of an emperor's bearing.

clue.text: People agree I improved the beastly place!

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: improved means reworked, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Visitors concur that the zoo has been smartened up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' usually means nasty; here it just means full of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show, so a place full of beasts.

clue.text: Author Archibald takes famous model to court

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the name receives the model inside it

parts.note: the usual short form of Archibald
the Model T Ford, the famous car
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A writer named Archibald sues over a celebrated fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' seems to describe Archibald, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is the creator or designer of a scheme, so its author in the sense of originator.

clue.text: Not a lot to eat? Exist without it!

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word sits around the second

parts.note: to exist is to be
taken as written

explanation.surface: Little food to hand? Then learn to get by without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is a small snack or mouthful, hardly a meal at all.

clue.text: Ask doctor when cold in bed

indicators.note: in places the cold abbreviation inside the reworked letters
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Consult your GP when you have a chill and are stuck in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sack is informal for bed, as in hitting the sack when going to sleep.

clue.text: See 1
Unusually stern Goths dropping round with gifts

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an odd order
dropping means letting go of, so the round letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Grim barbarians arrive laden with presents, an unlikely scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Strengths and gifts are both talents or natural abilities someone possesses.

clue.text: Cut and drilled without a ruler

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the ruler's letters are taken away

parts.note: drilled troops are exercised
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Soldiers trimmed and paraded with no monarch present.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Excised means removed by cutting, as a surgeon excises a growth.

clue.text: See 7
Small library opens with new title

indicators.note: opens with puts the library abbreviation at the front

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for library

indicators.note: new means made over, so the letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A modest local library opens with a newly released book.
explanation.definitionFit: Little and small are plain synonyms for something of limited size.

clue.text: Man in charge of a church

parts.note: a man's name
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is put in charge of a church, like a new vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often one granted special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Top worker comes back in for a doze

indicators.note: in means the worker is put inside the top

parts.note: a cap is a top, as of a bottle

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the worker is read backwards

parts.note: the worker ant is crossword shorthand for a worker

explanation.surface: The best employee returns home for a short sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top worker' reads as a star employee, but the two words are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a brief light sleep, the kind of doze taken in a chair.

clue.text: Certainly in time to obtain souvenir

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the time

parts.note: ten o'clock, a time
OK as agreement, certainly

explanation.surface: Arriving promptly will definitely secure you a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a keepsake or memento, an object kept as a reminder.

clue.text: Fifty one-cent promissory notes, filthy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for fifty
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A pile of tiny IOUs, grubby from handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Licentious means lewd and immoral, filthy in the sense of obscene or smutty.

clue.text: Some take Epsom salts to celebrate!

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: found across the two words
surface padding, completing the name of the purgative

explanation.surface: People dose themselves with Epsom salts, a purgative, as a festive treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate, taken as a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a festival is to observe or celebrate it, as in keeping Christmas.

clue.text: Crazy person, yet one using his head in a fight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a madman

definitions.text: one using his head in a fight
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who butts, from nut, slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: To nut someone is British slang for headbutting them, and the nut is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for a lunatic and, punningly, for someone who delivers a headbutt.

clue.text: He's handsome, but has bad back after a party

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

indicators.note: back means turned backwards, so the word for bad is read in reverse

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, something bad

explanation.surface: A good-looking man has a bad back after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name stands for any very handsome man.
